# Try to solve social golfers 10-5-6 using a SAT encoding with pysat
from pysat.solvers import Glucose4
from pysat.card import CardEnc, EncType
from pysat.formula import IDPool

G = 50  # golfers
S = 5   # group size
K = 10  # groups
W = 6   # weeks

vpool = IDPool()
# x[w][g][p] = 1 if golfer p in group g in week w
def x(w,g,p):
    return vpool.id(('x',w,g,p))

# y[w][p][q] = 1 if golfers p<q together in week w
def y(w,p,q):
    return vpool.id(('y',w,p,q))

solver = Glucose4()

# Each golfer in exactly one group per week
for w in range(W):
    for p in range(G):
        lits = [x(w,g,p) for g in range(K)]
        # exactly one
        cnf = CardEnc.equals(lits=lits, bound=1, vpool=vpool, encoding=EncType.pairwise)
        for cl in cnf.clauses:
            solver.add_clause(cl)

# Each group has exactly S golfers per week
for w in range(W):
    for g in range(K):
        lits = [x(w,g,p) for p in range(G)]
        cnf = CardEnc.equals(lits=lits, bound=S, vpool=vpool, encoding=EncType.seqcounter)
        for cl in cnf.clauses:
            solver.add_clause(cl)

# y[w,p,q] <=> exists g with x(w,g,p) and x(w,g,q)
# We need: if y=1 then sum over g of (x(w,g,p) AND x(w,g,q)) >= 1
# Simpler: define z(w,g,p,q) = x(w,g,p) AND x(w,g,q). Use y=OR of z.
# Then constraint sum_w y[w,p,q] <= 1.
# But we can avoid y by: for each pair (p,q), sum over w,g of z(w,g,p,q) <= 1.
# z(w,g,p,q) <=> x(w,g,p) & x(w,g,q). z -> x(w,g,p), z -> x(w,g,q), x&x -> z.
# Actually we just need sum_{w,g} (x(w,g,p)*x(w,g,q)) <= 1 which means pair together at most once.

# Using auxiliary z variables:
def z(w,g,p,q):
    return vpool.id(('z',w,g,p,q))

for p in range(G):
    for q in range(p+1,G):
        zlits = []
        for w in range(W):
            for g in range(K):
                zv = z(w,g,p,q)
                # z -> xp
                solver.add_clause([-zv, x(w,g,p)])
                solver.add_clause([-zv, x(w,g,q)])
                # xp & xq -> z
                solver.add_clause([-x(w,g,p), -x(w,g,q), zv])
                zlits.append(zv)
        # at most one
        cnf = CardEnc.atmost(lits=zlits, bound=1, vpool=vpool, encoding=EncType.seqcounter)
        for cl in cnf.clauses:
            solver.add_clause(cl)

print("Starting solve...")
import time
t=time.time()
res = solver.solve()
print("result:", res, "time:", time.time()-t)
